messages.subject: Divergence Rhat and n_eff
parts:
Hi Rstans users,

In looking the convergence of my estimations, I can say, the convergence is well with Rhat.
But with n_eff, the number is very small. The iteration is high 20000.

Could help me what I decide to my estimation.

Bests regard

Eric E.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Divergence Rhat and n_eff
parts:
On Saturday, June 18, 2016 at 11:15:42 AM UTC-4, Eric Innocents EBOULET wrote:
Hi Rstans users,

In looking the convergence of my estimations, I can say, the convergence is well with Rhat.
But with n_eff, the number is very small. The iteration is high 20000.

Could help me what I decide to my estimation.

Opinions differ. But even if you assume that the chains have all converged in distribution, then you cannot estimate functions of margins with a low effective sample size with much precision. Also, the estimator of effective sample size seems to be not very good when the true effective sample size is small or not well defined. I would think about reparameterizing your model.

Ben
